title: Pasta Bar Night
shortDescription: Choose-your-sauce pasta bar with garlic bread for ten
subtitle: Choose-your-sauce pasta bar with garlic bread for ten
description: A large batch of penne stays hot in a hotel pan while three sauces—marinara, Alfredo, and pesto—sit ready for crew to mix and match. Grated cheese, chili flakes, and garlic bread complete the bar.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Pasta Bar Night in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch vegetarian. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.instruction: Boil penne in well-salted water until just shy of al dente, about 9 minutes. Drain, toss with 2 tbsp olive oil, and hold covered in a hotel pan with a splash of reserved pasta water.

steps.title: Make Alfredo sauce
steps.instruction: Simmer cream with butter and minced garlic 3 minutes. Whisk in Parmesan until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon. Keep warm on lowest heat.

steps.title: Warm all sauces
steps.instruction: Heat marinara and pesto separately in saucepans until simmering. Stir Alfredo occasionally so it does not break. Verify all sauces reach 165°F for safe holding.

steps.title: Prepare garlic bread
steps.instruction: Split French bread, spread with butter and minced garlic, top with mozzarella, and bake at 375°F until golden and cheese melts, about 10 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F for any egg-based components. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Pasta Bar Night onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Set the pasta bar
steps.instruction: Line up pasta, three sauce pans with ladles, cheese, pepper flakes, and sliced garlic bread. Demonstrate mixing sauces—half marinara plus Alfredo is a crowd favorite.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Pasta Bar Night — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Reserve a cup of pasta water at the bar for loosening Alfredo if it tightens on hold.
Add grilled chicken strips as an optional protein upgrade without changing the bar format.
Label pesto 'contains nuts' if the crew includes allergy-sensitive members.
tonightSpread: Three-sauce pasta bar with garlic bread and simple Caesar salad.
Grated Parmesan and fresh basil in bowls for crews who want restaurant finish.
leftovers: Bake sauced pasta with extra cheese into a next-day casserole.
Toss cold pasta with olive oil, veggies, and feta for a lunch salad.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Pasta bar night is cheap, filling, and forgiving of late arrivals—sauce stays hot and pasta reheats well. Everyone customizes without cooking separate entrees for picky eaters.
mealPrepNotes: Cook pasta to just shy of al dente and toss with olive oil so it holds. Sauces can be made a day ahead and reheated gently. Reserve pasta water for adjusting sauce consistency at the bar.
